cases.name: reference-orders

views.label: Reference rows
views.note: The rows everything else points at, with their unique keys.

views.label: Checkout core
views.note: order is the hub: order_item and payment both point back at it.

views.label: Payment and stock
views.note: One optional dashed link and one mandatory stock link.

cards.title: Keys
items: Every child carries the parent id as a bigint foreign key.
order is the hub: order_item and payment each hold an order_id.
email and sku are unique, so they carry a secondary key marker.

cards.title: Optionality
items: An order may exist before any payment attempt, so the payment side is zero or many.
The payment relationship is non-identifying: it is drawn dashed.
customer, product, and order_item links are all mandatory.

cards.title: How the bands read
items: The checkout band is the order and the payment that settles it.
The catalog band is what orders point at: one product, one stock record.
accounts and line items stand alone; a single-table domain keeps its tag in the table header.

cases.name: reference-subscription-billing

views.label: Who belongs where
views.note: A user reaches a tenant through membership, which is why both ids are foreign keys on that table.

views.label: One invoice run
views.note: A subscription holds a price, an invoice holds its lines; the amount rolls up from the line.

views.label: Money in and back out
views.note: Payments are optional until a method is charged, and a refund only ever points at a captured payment.

cards.title: Scope
items: A redacted subscription-billing model: eleven tables, the fields the service actually stores.
Money is numeric(12,2) rather than float; every amount column records a currency or inherits one from price.
Timestamps are timestamptz, so an invoice keeps the instant it was issued, not a local reading of it.

cards.title: Optionality
items: An invoice may exist before a payment attempt, so the payment side is zero or many.
A refund is mandatory on its payment: nothing is refunded that was never captured.
membership carries both foreign keys; a user with no tenant has no membership row at all.
